items.note: PMG Unternehmen page: about 10,000 spaces in 25 facilities, eight owned, rest lease or management; MAG is parent company, MAG and Stadt Mainz are shareholders; about 2,300 spaces on the Universitaetsmedizin grounds; parking ticket valid as bus/tram fare of Mainzer Mobilitaet. Other PMG pages confirm the varying counts: 27 garages (31 March 2025 press release) and over 10,000 spaces in 28 facilities (40 Jahre page). Item wording is accurate. Operator facts rest on PMG's own site (self-description).

FAQ says the city has a parking guidance system, occupancy figures are sent regularly to the city so the free/occupied display rests on live data, a garage shown 'BESETZT' may still have spaces for permanent parkers, all garages are cashless except Rheinallee III, lost ticket 25 euro. All as written.

Mainz& page (May 2025): CityPort at Hauptbahnhof West switching to licence plate recognition, fully closed 12 May to 1 June 2025, per the city. The PMG 40 Jahre page says the first six garages were converted to plate recognition in 2024. Both claims match. The Mainz& article is dated 10 May 2025 and describes the closure as upcoming, which the item wording (closed from 12 May to 1 June) does not contradict; no page confirms it reopened on 1 June.

Checked the Kronberger Hof page and the Loehrstrasse, Rathaus, Deutschhausplatz, Bleiche, CityPort, Rheinufer, Schillerplatz, Taubertsberg, Theater, Schloss and Weisslilien pages: 6:00-19:00 first half hour 0.80, second and third half hour 1.00, fourth 1.10, from the third hour 2.10 per hour; daytime maximum 10.00; night 19:00-6:00 0.90 per half hour with 5.00 maximum. Same tariff on all of those pages. Pages are live tariff pages, undated (read 21 October 2026).

CineStar page: daytime maximum 15.50 (same half-hour tariff), 4.00 cinema tariff. Roemisches Theater page: maximum 15.50, but its day window is 8:00-20:00 and its tariff is 0.80 first half hour then 1.00 per half hour (not the standard structure). Gonsberg Campus: first hour 0.00, second hour 1.00, from the third hour 1.50 per hour, daytime maximum 8.00. Tiefgarage Weinlager: 1.00 per hour, 24.00 per 24 hours (also a 4.50 weekend rate). Parkhaus Wallstrasse: 303 spaces, 3.00 per 24 hours, weekend flat rate 6.00 (Saturday 8:00 to Monday 8:00), listed as outside the inner city. All as written. Cited URL covers only CineStar; the others were verified on their own PMG pages.

FAQ lists: event tariff 5 euro in Kronberger Hof, Theater and Parkplatz Schloss, Mon-Sat 18:00-8:00, Sunday 10:00-16:00; cinema tariff 4 euro at CineStar; swimming pool (Taubertsbergbad) 20 percent discount; Park&Go 10 percent on short-term tariffs. The offers page gives the Sunday window as 10:00-0:00 for the theatre tariff, so the Sunday end time differs between PMG pages (FAQ says 16:00, garage pages and offers page say 00:00); item follows the FAQ as stated.

PMG press release dated 31.03.2025: Park@Night announced for 1 July 2025; Haase and Steinkruger presented it with PMG director Sadowski; 16.99 per month Mon-Sat 17:00-9:00 and all day Sundays/holidays; 26.99 with all of Saturday; about 5,000 night spaces in participating garages; city to evaluate after three months. All as written. Note: Mainz& dated 28 March 2025 says the presentation took place on Friday 28 March; 31 March is the date of PMG's press release. Press release says 15 garages (plus perhaps 2-3). Announced, not yet in force on that date; item wording is correct.

PMG Angebote page: Park@Night 16.99 and Park@Night Plus 26.99 per month, 18 participating garages exactly as listed, prior Park&Go registration required, plate recognition or card, Park&Go 10 percent off. FAQ confirms 12-month contract with automatic renewal (and a one-time 9.99 euro activation fee, not mentioned in the item). Live undated page read 21 October 2026.

All 17 capacities match the individual PMG garage pages: CityPort 1105, Taubertsberg 767, Rheinufer 497, Rathaus 545, Kronberger Hof 460, Weisslilien 460, CineStar 459, Roemisches Theater 436, Schillerplatz 420, Gonsberg Campus 316, Wallstrasse 303, Bleiche 227, Theater 207, Deutschhausplatz 190, Weinlager 171, Loehrstrasse 145, Rheinallee III 94. However the cited overview URL (parkhaeuser-tarife) shows no capacities; the numbers are on each garage's own page. Parkplatz Schloss (122) not listed in the item; fine.

Mainz& (28 March 2025): Haase said the PMG garages, about 10,000 spaces, were at night only about 10 percent occupied. That was said at the presentation/announcement of Park@Night, not at its launch (the tariff started later, planned 1 July 2025). The 10 percent is the Lord Mayor's statement, not a published count. Sadowski said the earlier night tariff at 50-80 euro per month 'was not well accepted'; the 150-179 euro monthly price is for permanent bays, and the article does not say those were poorly accepted. The item wrongly applies 'not well accepted' to both.
items.corrected_text: At the presentation of the Park@Night tariff on 28 March 2025 (Mainz& report), Lord Mayor Nino Haase said the PMG garages, about 10,000 spaces, were at night only about 10 percent occupied (his statement, not a published count). PMG's director Ralf Sadowski said the earlier night tariff, at 50 to 80 euro per month, had not been well accepted; until then PMG's main product was permanent bays at 150 to 179 euro per month.

items.note: PMG press release dated 27.02.2026: 26 new charging points in Parkhaus Rathaus in service 'ab sofort', two accessible, described as the first accessible charging points in the Mainz urban area; power mostly from PMG's own PV system on the Rheingoldhalle roof; 54 cent per kWh including VAT; more charging places planned this year including Parkhaus Loehrstrasse. The split 24 on level 2 / 2 accessible on level 1 comes from the Rathaus garage page and FAQ rather than the press release; consistent.

Mainz& (1 July 2025, embedding a 21 March 2025 article): fees raised 1 July 2025 from 30 euro per year; formula 31.20 euro (0.60 x 52) times vehicle width times length; roughly 130 to 300 euro per year (article says 130 to more than 267, large vehicles possibly over 300); new permits valid at most one year; no social clause; 14,500 permits vs about 8,900 public spaces, about 25 zones, 7,600 permits in the Neustadt. NOT on the page: '60 euro for a two-year permit' (the page only says old permits were issued for two years and stay valid). Also the 14,500 permits and 7,600 in Neustadt are pre-increase figures ('bislang'). Single secondary source (Mainz& is an opinionated independent online paper; mainz.de returned 503, so the official ordinance was not checked).
items.corrected_text: Mainz raised resident parking permit fees on 1 July 2025, from 30 euro per year to a size-based formula (31.20 euro times vehicle width times length), giving roughly 130 to 300 euro per year; new permits are valid for at most one year, existing two-year permits stay valid, and the city said there would be no social discount. Before the increase the city counted about 14,500 permits against roughly 8,900 public spaces in about 25 resident zones, with about 7,600 permits in the Neustadt (regional press report, Mainz&).

items.note: Mainz& 12 September 2024: the city let the free-parking arrangement for e-cars lapse and announced it on Thursday; vehicles now need a parking ticket in public space except at charging stations; arrangement introduced 2017 for five years, extended in 2022 by council decision for two years; Mainz-registered electric and hybrid vehicles nearly 10 percent. All as written. Single secondary source; city press release not checked (mainz.de unavailable).

Mainz& 7 August 2026: since 1 August the Grosse Bleiche (near Landtag/Ernst-Ludwig-Platz, between Flachsmarkt and Peter-Altmeier-Allee) is closed to ordinary car traffic in the direction of the Rhine only; only buses, taxis and bicycles may pass. Council decided in June (2026) as a 'Modalfilter', justified by the capacity of the new tram line; the transport department claimed about 80 percent traffic reduction; detours via Bauhofstrasse and Flachsmarkt; the article reports confusion. The item omits that the closure is towards the Rhine and states the 80 percent as an expectation, which is correct. The article is strongly opinionated (headline, reader quotes); the 1 August closure date came before the 10 August tram opening. Single secondary source.
items.corrected_text: Mainz& reported on 7 August 2026 that since 1 August 2026 the Grosse Bleiche, between Flachsmarkt and Peter-Altmeier-Allee near the Landtag, is closed to ordinary car traffic in the direction of the Rhine; only buses, taxis and bicycles may pass. The city council had decided this in June 2026 as a 'Modalfilter' to protect the capacity of the new Binger Strasse tram link, and the transport department expects it to cut traffic there by about 80 percent. The paper reported confusion and detours via Bauhofstrasse and Flachsmarkt.

items.note: M wie Zukunft page: tram line Alicenplatz to Muensterplatz in service since 10 August 2026; line 53 from Lerchenberg now runs from Hauptbahnhof West through Binger Strasse to new stop Muensterplatz D; construction June 2024 to August 2026; status 'new line in operation'. NOT on the page: 'the street now has wider footways and cycle paths' (unsupported; the page instead notes on 30 June 2026 that the street stays single-lane for cars for now). Undated live page read 21 October 2026.
items.corrected_text: The new tram line through Binger Strasse (Alicenplatz to Muensterplatz) went into service on 10 August 2026; line 53 from Lerchenberg now runs from Hauptbahnhof West through Binger Strasse to the new stop Muensterplatz D. Construction ran from June 2024 to August 2026. A project news item of 30 June 2026 said the street would stay single-lane for car traffic for the time being.

items.note: M wie Zukunft Planungsstand page: since 9 April 2025 the decision is made (council followed the recommendation): Ludwigstrasse - Flachsmarkt - Grosse Bleiche - Rheinallee - Goethe- and Nahestrasse - Zollhafen. Timeline: planning approval procedure start end of 2027, approval and council construction decision early 2029, opening between 2032 and 2034. Item words it as a published timeline, which is correct. The page is undated and some of its timeline steps (mid-2025 completion of preliminary planning) are stale, so the 2032-2034 opening is a plan.

Mainz& 8 September 2026 on the IHK survey: 78 percent of firms rate the economic effects as mostly negative; four in five said access had worsened further since the last IHK survey in 2024; the car is a central factor for 94 percent of surveyed firms (the article also uses 94 percent for reliable commute being important, so it is inconsistent); Pendleratlas June 2025: about 80,000 in-commuters, 62.4 percent of about 128,000 employees subject to social insurance. Wording fixes: 'worsened since 2024' should be 'worsened further since the 2024 survey'; the commuter base is employees subject to social insurance, not all jobs; survey sample size and method not given and the survey was of IHK member firms. Mainz& is opinionated; the IHK release itself was not read.
items.corrected_text: An IHK Rheinhessen survey of its member firms, run in August 2026 and reported by Mainz& on 8 September 2026, found that 78 percent of responding firms rate the economic effect of the traffic situation as mostly negative, and four in five said access to their site had worsened further since the previous IHK survey in 2024. The car is a central factor for reaching the city centre for 94 percent of surveyed firms (sample size not given). Federal Pendleratlas figures cited in the article give about 80,000 in-commuters, 62.4 percent of roughly 128,000 employees subject to social insurance, in June 2025.

items.note: Mainz& 19 July 2019: the city commissioned a study in 2018 for three pre-set sites; the largest potential was at the Hechtsheim end, 70 to 110 spaces, counting work commuters only (shoppers and visitors not included); city spokesman said up to 200 commuter spaces could be created in the old garage at Kurmainz-Kaserne, negotiations underway. The 'only existing P+R lot at the Hechtsheim terminus' is the journalist's statement, not attributed to the city. Item wrongly says the study was in 2019 (commissioned 2018, reported 2019) and 'only about' understates that it was the best-rated area. Old article; no current capacity.
items.corrected_text: In a July 2019 article, Mainz& reported on a study the city had commissioned in 2018 for three pre-set sites: its largest potential was at the Hechtsheim end of the tram, with demand for about 70 to 110 park-and-ride spaces counting work commuters only. The city said it was negotiating for up to 200 commuter spaces in the old garage at the Kurmainz-Kaserne, and the paper noted the only existing park-and-ride lot was at the Hechtsheim tram terminus. This is a 2019 account, not current capacity.

corrected_summary: Mainz's central garages are run mostly by the municipal PMG Parken in Mainz GmbH (shareholders: the Mainzer Aufbaugesellschaft and the city), which says it has about 10,000 spaces in 25 facilities on its company page (its other pages say 27 or 28). Typical PMG city-centre tariffs, read on 21 October 2026, are 0.80 euro for the first half hour and a 10.00 euro daytime maximum, with 15.50 euro at Roemisches Theater and CineStar and 3.00 euro per 24 hours at Parkhaus Wallstrasse. PMG announced a Park@Night tariff in March 2025 for July 2025; its offers page now lists it at 16.99 euro per month in 18 garages. The city parking guidance shows free or occupied status based on live garage data, and PMG put 26 charging points into service at Parkhaus Rathaus in February 2026. On the street, according to regional press (Mainz&), resident permit fees rose on 1 July 2025 from 30 euro to roughly 130 to 300 euro per year and free parking for electric cars ended in September 2024. The tram link through Binger Strasse opened on 10 August 2026, and from 1 August 2026 the Grosse Bleiche has been closed to ordinary car traffic towards the Rhine; the inner-city tram route was decided in April 2025 with opening planned for 2032 to 2034. An IHK survey reported by Mainz& says building sites and traffic changes hurt city-centre access, and park-and-ride in Mainz is minor: a 2019 report on a 2018 study saw demand for about 70 to 110 work-commuter spaces at the Hechtsheim end of the tram. Mainz has roughly 80,000 in-commuters (June 2025). Official mainz.de pages were not available (HTTP 503).
